input.question: Was Pangaea an accident or necessary?
input.ground_truth: Sure it would be possible for there to be multiple continents without having a Pangea first. It is possible to have a world with absolutely no active tectonics. In fact Earth may be very unusual in this respect, we don't know yet. A super continent is in no way a prerequisite for separate continents to eventually exist, it is just the way it happened on our planet to the best of our knowledge. Also our separate continents may eventually combine again to become a second Pangea.

Okay! Imagine Earth is like a big puzzle. Long, long ago, all the puzzle pieces (which are now continents like Africa, America, and Asia) were stuck together to make one big piece called Pangaea.

Now, was it an accident or did it have to happen?

Well, it wasn’t on purpose. It wasn’t like Earth said, “Let’s make one big land!” It just happened because of how the Earth moves inside. The Earth’s inside is really hot and moves around, and that makes the puzzle pieces move and stick together sometimes and then split apart later. So, Pangaea happened by accident because of the way the Earth works, not because it had to be that way every time. It just happened that way one time!
